answer:
Hypothesis (data-grounded answer): In the surveyed ML-enabled system projects, the two least-used documentation formats for requirements are (1) BDD (Behavior-Driven Development) scenarios and (2) the ML Canvas. Among the 194 survey respondents who answered the documentation question (82 further respondents were excluded because they carried the -77 skip sentinel, aligned with suspended survey status), only 4/194 (2.06%, bootstrap 95% CI [0.52%, 4.12%]) indicated using BDD scenarios and 15/194 (7.73%, 95% CI [4.12%, 11.86%]) indicated using the ML Canvas — far below ubiquitous formats such as notebooks (34.02%), user stories (32.47%) and requirements lists (26.29%). We therefore hypothesize that lightweight, structured/ML-specific notation formats (BDD scenarios and ML Canvas) are rarely adopted for documenting requirements in ML-enabled system projects, with practitioners defaulting to general-purpose artifacts (notebooks, user stories, requirements lists) instead. Transparency note on the tie: the free-text catch-all category "Others" is also quoted by exactly 15/194 respondents (7.73%, CI [4.12%, 11.86%]); since it aggregates miscellaneous ad-hoc artifacts (Jira/Confluence pages, wikis, meeting notes) rather than a named format, ML Canvas is reported as the second-least-used named format, but it is statistically tied with "Others" and with Vision Documents / Goal Models (29/194, 14.95%) within bootstrap uncertainty.

Percentage reconciliation (explicit pass, as requested): none of the tested aggregations reproduces both targets, 10.13% [9.926, 10.333] and 4.366% [4.231, 4.501]:
 (a) denominator 276 with -77 as non-use: BDD 1.449%, ML Canvas/Others 5.435% (two lowest unchanged: BDD Scenarios, ML Canvas); Vision/Goal Models reach 10.507% — close to 10.13% but not a match, and nothing lands at 4.366%.
 (b) quoted / total quoted selections (total = 416): Prototypes = 10.096% is near 10.13%, but no count over 416 gives 4.366% (closest: ML Canvas/Others at 3.606%); this aggregation would in any case not rank Prototypes as "least used", so it is internally inconsistent with the question.
 (c) denominator = respondents quoting ≥1 format (174): BDD 2.30%, ML Canvas 8.62% — no match.
 (d) inverse-frequency weighting (respondent weight 1/#formats-quoted): BDD 0.56%, ML Canvas 2.53%, Goal Models 4.29%, Others 4.42% — Goal Models/Others brush against 4.366%, but the same weighting gives nothing at 10.13% and breaks the monotone ranking, so it is not a coherent generator of both targets.
 (e) exhaustive fraction search (counts 1–80 over plausible denominators 194, 276, 174, 416, 164, 188, 148, 2328, 498): zero fractions match 10.13% or 4.366% to within ±0.005 pp.
 (f)/(g) bootstrap means equal the raw proportions (e.g., BDD 2.048%, ML Canvas 7.756%) and, at n = 194, bootstrap CIs are ±3–4 pp wide — structurally incompatible with the targets' ±0.2 pp CIs; the target CIs imply an effective sample on the order of 10^4–10^5, which this dataset cannot produce.
Plain conclusion: the two gold percentages (and their extremely narrow CIs) cannot be derived from the supplied CSV under any natural aggregation; they most plausibly originate from the original study's raw ordinal (Likert degree-of-use) coding, which was binarized to "quoted"/"not quoted" in this file. The hypothesis is therefore grounded in the computed rates and the robust, aggregation-invariant rank ordering (BDD Scenarios last under every tested scheme; ML Canvas second-last under every scheme except the tie-with-Others), not in force-fit numbers.

payload.hypothesis: The two least-used documentation formats for requirements in ML-enabled system projects are BDD scenarios (4/194 = 2.06%, bootstrap 95% CI [0.52%, 4.12%]) and the ML Canvas (15/194 = 7.73%, 95% CI [4.12%, 11.86%]). Practitioners rarely adopt these structured/ML-specific notations, defaulting instead to notebooks (34.02%), user stories (32.47%) and requirements lists (26.29%). Caveats reported transparently: the free-text catch-all 'Others' category ties ML Canvas exactly (15/194, CI [4.12%, 11.86%]) and is treated as a non-named format; ML Canvas is statistically tied with Vision Documents/Goal Models (14.95%) within bootstrap uncertainty. The stated target percentages (10.13% and 4.366%, with ±0.2 pp CIs) could not be reproduced from the supplied binary quoted/not-quoted data under any tested aggregation (denominator 276/194/174/416, share-of-total-selections, inverse-frequency weighting, bootstrap means, exhaustive fraction search); they most likely derive from the original study's ordinal degree-of-use coding, which is not present in this CSV. The rank ordering itself is robust across all tested aggregations.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded the 276x202 CSV; confirmed all 12 substantive Q10_ML_Documentation_* columns are binary categorical ('quoted'/'not quoted'/'-77'), not Likert. 2) Excluded the 82 respondents with the -77 skip sentinel (aligned with Status='Suspended'), leaving n=194. 3) Coded usage as a binary indicator ('quoted') and computed per-format usage rates. 4) Bootstrapped the 194 respondents with replacement, B=10,000, seed=42, percentile 95% CIs. 5) Ranked formats ascending; identified BDD Scenarios (2.06%) and ML Canvas (7.73%) as least used, handling the MLCanvas/Others tie in favor of the named format and reporting it explicitly. 6) Ran a reconciliation pass against the target percentages testing five alternative aggregations (denominator 276 with -77 as non-use; share of 416 total quoted selections; denominator of 174 respondents quoting >=1 format; inverse-frequency weighting; exhaustive small-fraction search plus bootstrap-mean comparison) — none reproduces both 10.13% and 4.366% or their narrow CIs, so the answer is grounded in the computed rates and the aggregation-invariant rank ordering.
payload.reconciliation_outcome: No tested aggregation reproduces both target percentages and their narrow CIs; targets most plausibly stem from the original ordinal data, not supplied binary CSV.
